facts.text: Highland Park’s ravine on Nose Hill’s southern slope is a prominent geographical landmark that once guided early farmers and later became a golf course.
McKnight Boulevard, named after WWII Battle of Britain pilot William McKnight, runs along Highland Park’s northern boundary.
The historic Centre Street North was once part of Calgary’s streetcar network, linking Highland Park’s 32nd Avenue station to downtown.
Highland Park was annexed in 1910 and grew rapidly during the 1940s‑50s oil boom, transforming from homesteads to a suburban community.
The industrial area that once belonged to Highland Park is now known as Greenview Industrial, yet locals still consider it part of the neighbourhood.
A steep escarpment on the eastern edge of Highland Park’s plateau physically bisects the residential area, creating a dramatic skyline.
